narrative.summaryIntro:
Brihadeeswarar Temple (also known as Periya Koil) in Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a masterpiece of Chola period architecture. Built by Raja Raja Chola I in 1010 CE, the temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva as Brihadeeswarar (Great Lord). The temple's towering vimana (spire) stands at 216 feet and is constructed with granite, representing the pinnacle of medieval South Indian temple architecture.

The temple is renowned for its magnificent stone carvings, sculptures, and architectural innovations that influenced temple construction for centuries. The massive vimana is one of the tallest structures built in the 11th century and is a remarkable feat of ancient engineering. The temple complex features elaborate gopurams, sacred tanks, and ornate pillared halls. It remains one of the greatest monuments of the Chola dynasty and a testament to Hindu artistic and spiritual excellence.
